stem: A clinical research study measures treatment response rate across 3 trial sites, each containing multiple patient cohorts. trial site A has 5 observations with mean 52.4 % (within-trial site SD = 7.1). trial site B has 8 observations with mean 67.0 % (within-trial site SD = 7.2). trial site C has 5 observations with mean 86.3 % (within-trial site SD = 6.7). The between-trial site standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 5.8 and 14.4 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true treatment response rate for trial site C, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-trial site variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for trial site C: 84.7 % (shrunk from raw 86.3). Range [82.5, 85.6] as between-trial site SD varies from 5.8 to 14.4. Pooled mean: 68.3.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 68.3 % (weighted average of 3 trial site means).
Shrinkage factor for trial site C: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=9.6: B = 0.911.
Interval [82.5, 85.6] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (86.3) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (68.3) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
